# International climate finance: pricing

*Generated by `index/tools/climate-portfolio/international.py` from `international.json`; do not edit by hand. Read with [climate-portfolio-international.md](climate-portfolio-international.md). 2025 dollars; low / mid / high.*

## The 2035 gap after domestic action

- Package A (as approved) in the carbon model: 47.5% below 2005 in net greenhouse gases in 2035.
- Plus CLI-13 farms, forests and removal (outside the model): 60 / 135 / 250 Mt, giving 48.4 / 49.6 / 51.3% domestically.
- Gap to 61%: 632 / 747 / 822 Mt a year in 2035; gap to 66%: 959 / 1,074 / 1,149 Mt.

## What verified mitigation abroad could supply in 2035

| Source | Mt CO2e a year, 2035 | Price, $/t | Cost in 2035, $B (with integrity reserve) | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Oil, gas and coal-mine methane abroad: results payments to producers and regulators, verified by satellite and measurement | 100 / 200 / 350 | 8 / 15 / 25 | 0.9 / 3.8 / 12.2 | estimate: the IEA finds about 70% of fossil methane (nearly 85 Mt CH4, roughly 2.4 Gt CO2e) abatable with existing technology and about 30% (35 Mt CH4) at no net cost at 2025 prices (Global Methane Tracker 2026). Payments buy speed and verification where capital, not price, is the barrier; no-cost tons raise additionality questions, so they need jurisdiction-wide baselines |
| Jurisdictional forest results (national or state programs, ART-TREES style), with Indigenous and local community safeguards | 50 / 150 / 300 | 12 / 20 / 35 | 0.7 / 3.8 / 14.7 | sourced range: LEAF Coalition purchases jurisdictional credits, reported $10 a ton floor; Nepal's January 2026 agreement is up to 4 Mt for up to $55M (about $14 a ton); Ghana and Costa Rica (2023) over $60M. Jurisdictional accounting addresses leakage better than project credits; permanence needs buffers |
| Early coal retirement and grid results contracts (Energy Transition Mechanism and JETP style) | 50 / 100 / 200 | 15 / 30 / 50 | 0.8 / 3.8 / 14.0 | estimate: ADB's first ETM deal (Cirebon-1, 660 MW) targets retirement in 2035 instead of 2042 and up to 30 Mt avoided over 15 years; its financial terms are undisclosed |
| Article 6.2 programs: renewables, efficiency, e-mobility and industry, bilateral with corresponding adjustments | 20 / 50 / 100 | 30 / 40 / 60 | 0.7 / 2.5 / 8.4 | sourced: Switzerland's bilateral purchases about $36 a ton; vendor indications $30-50. As of May 2026, 128 bilateral agreements but only five completed transfers (65,000 ITMOs): the market barely exists yet |
| Durable removals abroad (biochar, mineral weathering, direct air capture) | 5 / 10 / 30 | 100 / 150 / 250 | 0.6 / 1.9 / 10.5 | estimate: durable removal prices remain $100s a ton; direct air capture projected at $230-540 a ton by 2050 (ETH Zurich 2024) |

**Together:** 225 / 510 / 980 Mt in 2035 (3.4 / 7.8 / 15.0 points of the 2005 baseline), at an average 16 / 31 / 61 $/t including the integrity reserve (10 / 25 / 40%). Cost in 2035: 3.6 / 15.6 / 59.8 $B. Combined with domestic action at the mid case: 53.0 / 57.4 / 64.6% below 2005.

**2030-39**, ramping from 10% of the 2035 volume in 2030: 1.6 / 3.7 / 7.2 Gt bought for 26 / 114 / 437 $B (2025 dollars), 0.033 / 0.144 / 0.552 $T nominal.

**Beside it, counted as climate finance but never toward emissions:** loss and damage 10 / 20 / 30 $B and adaptation above DEV-P 20 / 40 / 60 $B over 2030-39.

Context: sourced: COP29's new goal is at least $300B a year by 2035 from developed countries; ODI puts a U.S. fair share at about 45% of developed-country obligations (that share counts public and mobilized private and multilateral money). WRI put the U.S. share of the earlier $100B goal at 40-47%. From sources/climate-portfolio-packages.json diagnostics: beyond Package A, the next domestic steps (clean-heat standard, 50% industrial support, a $200 price, coal by 2032) add about one point in 2035 for about $160B more outlays over 2030-39 and several dollars a month on bills.
